questions.question: Antifreeze helps keep an engine working properly:

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
When it is both cold and hot outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is both cold and hot outside.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's cooling system needs enough water and antifreeze. Antifreeze helps the engine work well in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: After you start the engine, the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on if:

options.text: The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn on when you start the engine, then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working right.

questions.question: Once cargo is secured on a vehicle:

options.text: You do not need to inspect it.
You should not let others inspect it.
You should check it every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check it every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or three hours after that.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose grip on the road.
The trailer disconnects from the truck.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, the engine must be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a regular car driver.
Not worry about speed, just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not know how slowly you need to turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil on the road. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection:

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report only matters if you have passengers.
You should review the last inspection report if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should review the last inspection report if there is one.
questions.explanation: Start by reviewing the last vehicle inspection report. Only sign the current report if any defects noted before have been fixed.

questions.question: When driving a triple on a mountain road, you:

options.text: Do not need to worry about the terrain.
Should drive at or above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be extra careful.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers need extra caution on mountains. They pull more weight and length, which makes them more likely to skid or lose grip.

questions.question: Look ahead at the road for ____.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards and react to them. Watch for vehicles entering the highway or moving into your lane.

questions.question: Before inspecting your vehicle, look under it to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on a slope.
Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspection, check your vehicle's condition. Look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for anything that could block movement, like people, other vehicles, or hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Keep the cab cool using air conditioning or open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool using air conditioning or open a window.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue while driving, keep the cab cool with air conditioning or an open window. Avoid heavy foods. Take rest breaks every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Never touch each other.
questions.explanation: During inspection, check that your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: A commercial vehicle must have:

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light might be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving. A driver who has used alcohol, is sleepy, or is on drugs may stop at wrong places, like green lights.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is better because:

options.text: Turning the other way is illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see better.
questions.explanation: When backing, turn toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: After a pre-trip inspection, make sure the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the emergency and service line valves to check that air reaches all brakes. You will hear air escaping. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope it goes away.
Write a report describing the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving day, write a report about any vehicle problems. Note any issues that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.
